issues.legal_issue: A person defending possession of property may use force causing death when a forcible attempt to take the property is accompanied by an assault creating a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt, and the defender does not exceed the right of private defence.
material_facts: The accused were in possession of the land and had grown the ripe paddy crop on it.
The deceased and their group trespassed onto the land and attempted to harvest the crop.
The deceased and their group were the aggressors and used sharp cutting weapons against the accused.
Two accused were first attacked and sustained grievous injuries from sharp weapons, including injuries to vital parts of the body.
The attack occurred before the attackers had retreated.
The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court reversed the acquittal and convicted three of them of culpable homicide.
issues.conclusion: The accused were entitled to exercise private defence of both person and property, and that right extended to causing death in the circumstances. They had not exceeded that right. The High Court's reversal was set aside and the trial court's acquittal was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 97 and 99 of the Indian Penal Code, the right of private defence extends to the body and property, subject to the restrictions in Section 99. Under Section 100, the right of defence of the body may extend to voluntarily causing death where an assault may reasonably cause apprehension of death or grievous hurt. Under Section 103, the right of defence of property may extend to causing death in specified circumstances, including theft or mischief where a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt would otherwise arise. A person in possession may use reasonable force to keep away a trespasser; where the facts establish a qualifying threat and the attackers have not retreated, the defender does not exceed the right by causing death. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_reversal_of_acquittal and accused_possessed_property_and_crop and trespassers_attempted_to_take_crop and trespassers_used_force_first and sharp_weapons_caused_grievous_injuries_to_vital_parts and attackers_had_not_withdrawn

predicates.appeal_challenges_reversal_of_acquittal: The case is an appeal challenging a higher court's reversal of an acquittal.
predicates.accused_possessed_property_and_crop: The accused possessed the property and had grown the crop on it.
predicates.trespassers_attempted_to_take_crop: Trespassers entered the property and attempted to take the crop.
predicates.trespassers_used_force_first: The trespassers initiated the violence against the accused.
predicates.sharp_weapons_caused_grievous_injuries_t: The trespassers used sharp weapons to inflict grievous injuries on vital parts of the accused's bodies.
predicates.attackers_had_not_withdrawn: The attackers had not retreated when the accused used force.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the reversal of an acquittal and the accused possessed the property and crop, trespassers attempted to take the crop and used force first, sharp weapons caused grievous injuries to vital parts, and the attackers had not withdrawn, the acquittal is upheld.
